mainTopic: הפסק after המוציא, health advice for meals, רבי יהודה's ברכה on greens, and which mistaken ברכות still count
overview: The גמרא first discusses which words spoken between המוציא and eating the bread count as an interruption. רב, רבי יוחנן, and רב ששת each draw that line in a different place. Next comes a series of teachings from רבא בר שמואל in the name of רבי חייא: wait for salt before breaking bread (unless the bread is fine), plus advice about urinating and about finishing meals with salt and water. The גמרא then lists more health advice about water, lentils, mustard, small fish, and black cumin. For black cumin, it resolves a contradiction: its smell is harmful, but its taste is healing. It returns to the משנה, rules that the הלכה is not like רבי יהודה's special ברכה for greens, and explains his reasoning from 'ברוך ה׳ יום יום'. After a short aggadic teaching that a 'full vessel' of Torah holds more, a new משנה teaches which mistaken ברכות still count after the fact. The גמרא links this to רבי יהודה's views: that a tree is part of the ground, and that wheat is called a 'tree'. It begins to define when בורא פרי העץ is said, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב: Which words interrupt between the ברכה and eating
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that saying 'take, the blessing was made' is not a הפסק. Asking for salt or relish is a הפסק and requires a new ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: If someone broke bread and said 'Take, the blessing was made; take, the blessing was made,' he does not need to bless again. If he said 'Bring salt' or 'Bring relish,' he must bless again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's rule about what kind of talking between the ברכה and eating forces a person to repeat the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words that are directly about the ברכה itself, like handing out pieces of the blessed bread, are not an interruption. רב treats asking for salt or relish as a separate request, so it breaks the link between the ברכה and the eating. This is the strictest of the three opinions in this discussion. The next two steps bring the other two, רבי יוחנן and רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Take, it was blessed' — handing out the blessed bread
Relish or side dish eaten with bread

steps.confusionAlert: This is about talking AFTER saying המוציא and BEFORE eating. It is not about talking in the middle of the meal.

phrases.english: Rav said: 'Take, it is blessed; take, it is blessed' —
phrases.notes: Said while handing out pieces of the bread right after the blessing

phrases.english: he does not need to bless again.
'Bring salt,' 'Bring relish' —
he must bless again.
phrases.notes: In רב's view this counts as an interruption

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the topic of הפסק between the ברכה and eating
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Speech about the blessed bread is not a הפסק. Requesting salt or relish is a הפסק.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Salt is fine, but feeding oxen interrupts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן is more lenient. Asking for salt or relish is not a הפסק, but telling someone to mix food for the oxen is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Even if he said 'Bring salt' or 'Bring relish,' he does not need to bless again. If he said 'Mix feed for the oxen, mix feed for the oxen,' he must bless again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב and moves the line further. Salt and relish are part of the bread meal, but animal feed is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, anything that helps the bread-eating itself, like salt or relish, belongs to the ברכה. Preparing food for animals has nothing to do with his own eating, so it breaks the connection.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even 'Bring salt,' 'Bring relish'
also does not require blessing again;
'Mix for the oxen, mix for the oxen' —
he must bless again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב and is more lenient about salt and relish
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Requests for salt or relish are not a הפסק. Instructions to feed the oxen are a הפסק.

steps.title: רב ששת: Even feeding oxen does not interrupt
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת is the most lenient. Even telling someone to mix food for the oxen is not a הפסק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Even 'Mix feed for the oxen' does not require him to bless again.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת goes further than רבי יוחנן and says even the oxen instruction is not an interruption. The next step gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a third position on the same scale. רב ששת holds that feeding one's animals is part of the process of one's own meal, which the next step explains.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet said:
Even 'Mix for the oxen'
also does not require blessing again,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבי יוחנן's leniency even further
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even instructions to feed the animals are not a הפסק.

steps.title: Source: One must feed his animals before eating
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's view is supported by רב's teaching, based on a פסוק, that a person may not eat before feeding his animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A person may not eat before he gives food to his animal, as it says, 'And I will give grass in your field for your animals,' and only afterward, 'and you will eat and be satisfied.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב ששת says feeding the oxen is not an interruption. Feeding the animals is actually a required step before one's own meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first mentions food for the animals and only then the person eating. So feeding them is a halachic first step of one's own meal. It therefore belongs to the ברכה and is not an interruption.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forbidden for a person
And you will eat and be satisfied

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on הפסק after המוציא: רב (salt interrupts), רבי יוחנן (only oxen interrupts), רב ששת (even oxen does not interrupt, because feeding animals comes first by law).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the well-known source for the halacha that one feeds one's animals before eating.

phrases.english: For Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
It is forbidden for a person to eat
before he gives food to his animal,
as it says: 'And I will give grass in your field for your animals'
and only afterward: 'and you shall eat and be satisfied.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב ששת's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's ruling that feeding the oxen is not a הפסק
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's teaching from the פסוק 'ונתתי עשב בשדך לבהמתך ואכלת ושבעת'

steps.title: Wait for salt before breaking bread
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שמואל in the name of רבי חייא rules that the one making המוציא should not break the bread until salt or relish is in front of everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר שמואל said in the name of רבי חייא: The one breaking the bread may not break it until salt or relish has been brought before each and every person.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: the person breaking the bread must wait until salt or relish is on the table for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once salt or relish is ready, everyone can eat right after the ברכה without any delay. This also connects to the earlier discussion, since it prevents the need to ask for salt after the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who breaks the bread

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rava bar Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
The one breaking bread is not permitted to break it
until they bring salt or relish
before each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New teaching on a related topic: preparing the meal before breaking bread
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not break the bread until salt or relish is in front of everyone.

steps.title: רבא בר שמואל broke bread without waiting
steps.stepSummary: At the house of the ריש גלותא, רבא בר שמואל broke the bread right away. People asked him whether he had retracted his own ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר שמואל came to the house of the ריש גלותא. They brought him bread, and he broke it immediately. They said to him: Has the Master retracted his teaching?
steps.whatsHappening: A story seems to contradict the rule just taught, and the people present challenge רבא בר שמואל about it. The next step is his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His own action looks like it goes against what he taught in the name of רבי חייא. The question asks whether he changed his mind or whether the rule has limits.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, head of the Jews in Bavel
Has the master retracted his teaching?

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל אִקְּלַע לְבֵי רֵישׁ גָּלוּתָא,
phrases.english: Rava bar Shmuel happened to come to the house of the Exilarch,
they brought out bread for him,
and he broke it right away.
They said to him: Has the master retracted his teaching?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 5 from רבא בר שמואל's own behavior
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one must wait for salt before breaking bread
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The teacher of the rule acted against it himself

steps.title: Fine bread does not need to wait for salt
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שמואל answers that this fine bread does not need salt, so there is no need to wait.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This bread does not require waiting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר שמואל explains that the rule only applies to bread that needs salt for flavor. The ריש גלותא's high-quality bread is tasty on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of waiting stays in force. It just does not apply here, because the reason for waiting is that plain bread needs salt to taste good. Fine bread does not, so he could break it right away.
steps.whatToRemember: One waits for salt before breaking bread only when the bread needs it for taste. Fine bread does not require waiting.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֵית דֵּין צְרִיךְ בְּשַׁשׁ.
phrases.english: He said to them: This one does not require waiting.
phrases.notes: Refined bread is tasty without salt

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֵית דֵּין צְרִיךְ בְּשַׁשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (the rule depends on the type of bread)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed he had dropped the rule of waiting for salt
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies only to bread that needs salt. Fine bread is an exception.

steps.title: Urine fully leaves only when sitting
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שמואל in the name of רבי חייא says urine fully empties only when one is seated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא בר שמואל said in the name of רבי חייא: Urine is completely emptied only when sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with another teaching from the same chain, רבא בר שמואל quoting רבי חייא. This one is about health and hygiene.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who stands worries about splashing his clothes, so he stops too early and does not empty fully. Sitting removes that worry.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: And Rava bar Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Chiya:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מֵי רַגְלַיִם כָּלִים אֶלָּא בִּישִׁיבָה.
phrases.english: Urine is completely emptied only when sitting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, unrelated teaching grouped by the same speaker
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urine fully leaves the body only when sitting.

steps.title: רב כהנא: Standing is fine over loose soil or a slope
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא adds that over loose soil one may stand. Without loose soil, one should stand on a high spot and urinate down a slope.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: And over loose soil, even standing is fine. If there is no loose soil, he should stand in a high place and urinate down a slope.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא qualifies the previous teaching by giving cases where standing works just as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern behind the previous rule is splashing. Loose soil absorbs the urine, and a downward slope carries it away. Either one removes the worry, so standing is fine.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: And over loose soil,
even while standing.
And if there is no loose soil,
he should stand in a high place
and urinate down a slope.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies step 8 with cases where standing is fine
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Standing is fine over loose soil, or from a high place down a slope.

steps.title: Eat salt after food and drink water after drinks
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שמואל in the name of רבי חייא advises eating salt after every meal and drinking water after every drink, to avoid harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא בר שמואל said in the name of רבי חייא: After all your eating, eat salt; after all your drinking, drink water; and you will not be harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: A third teaching from רבא בר שמואל quoting רבי חייא, giving health advice about finishing meals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is practical health guidance, not a ברכה law. Salt after food and water after other drinks protect a person from harm.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: And Rava bar Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Chiya:
After all your eating, eat salt,
and after all your drinking, drink water,
and you will not be harmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same speaker
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salt after eating and water after drinking prevent harm.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with the exact same wording, supporting רבא בר שמואל's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: After all your eating, eat salt; after all your drinking, drink water; and you will not be harmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא, a source from the time of the תנאים, says the same advice word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תניא נמי הכי' means 'it was also taught this way.' It confirms that רבא בר שמואל's teaching has an earlier source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: The wording repeats on purpose. The גמרא is quoting a separate source that matches, not repeating itself by mistake.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
After all your eating, eat salt,
and after all your drinking, drink water,
and you will not be harmed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 10 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רבא בר שמואל's advice about salt and water

steps.title: Another ברייתא: the dangers of skipping salt and water
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא describes what happens if one skips salt or water. By day he should worry about bad breath, and at night about אסכרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא taught: If one ate any food and did not eat salt, or drank any drink and did not drink water — by day he should worry about bad breath, and at night he should worry about diphtheria.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that spells out the harm the advice protects against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first sources only said 'you will not be harmed.' This ברייתא names the specific harms: bad breath during the day and the dangerous illness אסכרה at night.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא בר שמואל in the name of רבי חייא taught three things: wait for salt before breaking bread (unless the bread is fine), sitting helps urine empty fully, and finish meals with salt and drinks with water.

phrases.english: Another ברייתא taught:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל כׇּל מַאֲכָל וְלֹא אָכַל מֶלַח,
phrases.english: If he ate any food and did not eat salt,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁתָה כׇּל מַשְׁקִין וְלֹא שָׁתָה מַיִם,
phrases.english: or drank any drinks and did not drink water,
by day — he should worry about bad breath,
and at night — he should worry about diphtheria.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ברייתא that adds the specific dangers
steps.raayaObject: The advice to eat salt and drink water after meals
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second ברייתא describing the harms of skipping them

steps.title: A ברייתא: Drinking Plenty of Water With Food Protects the Intestines
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who drinks a lot of water with his food will not suffer from intestinal illness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Someone who 'floods' his food with water will not come to suffer from intestinal sickness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא that adds another health tip about drinking water with meals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא בר שמואל taught that one should drink water after every drink. This ברייתא adds a separate tip: drinking plenty of water while eating protects the intestines. The image is food that 'floats' in water.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes something float, meaning one who floods it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who floods his food with water,
phrases.notes: He drinks a lot of water with his meal.

phrases.english: will not come to suffer intestinal illness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another health ברייתא about water, continuing the theme of steps 10-12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drinking plenty of water with food prevents intestinal illness.

steps.title: How Much Water Is Needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much water counts as 'flooding' the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question about the ברייתא: how much water is meant. This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said to 'flood' the food but gave no amount. The question is not an attack; it only asks for a clear measure.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure missing from the ברייתא in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of water needed to count as 'flooding' the food.

steps.title: רב חסדא: One Jug of Water Per Loaf
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the amount is one jug of water for each loaf of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: one jug of water for each loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by giving a measure: one jug of water for every loaf eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the general advice into a practical amount. The amount of water depends on how much bread one eats.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
One jug per loaf.
phrases.notes: One jug of water for each loaf of bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One jug of water per loaf of bread.

steps.title: Lentils Once a Month Protect the Household From Diphtheria
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי in the name of רבי יוחנן says that eating lentils once every thirty days keeps אסכרה away from one's home, but not every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Someone who regularly eats lentils once every thirty days keeps אסכרה (a deadly throat disease) out of his house. But not every day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new health teaching: lentils eaten once a month protect the home from אסכרה. The גמרא adds that one should not eat them daily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The benefit depends on how often one eats them. Once a month helps, but every day does not. The reason for the daily limit comes in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מָרִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Mari said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who regularly eats lentils once in thirty days
keeps diphtheria away from his house.
But every day — no.
phrases.notes: One should not eat lentils daily.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מָרִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָרָגִיל בַּעֲדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new health tip, about lentils, within the same list of advice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lentils once every thirty days prevent אסכרה in the home, but they should not be eaten daily.

steps.title: Why Not Eat Lentils Every Day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why lentils should not be eaten every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the limit on eating lentils daily. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lentils are healthy, eating more of them might seem even better. The question asks what harm comes from eating them every day.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the daily limit in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why lentils should not be eaten every day.

steps.title: Daily Lentils Cause Bad Breath
steps.stepSummary: Eating lentils every day causes bad breath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is harmful, causing bad breath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that eating lentils daily causes bad breath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The once-a-month benefit stays in place. The daily limit exists only because steady use brings a side effect, bad breath.

keyTerms.meaning: Smell of the mouth, bad breath

phrases.english: Because it is harmful, causing bad breath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.

steps.title: Mustard Once a Month Protects the Household From Illness
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי in the name of רבי יוחנן also says that mustard once every thirty days keeps illnesses away from the home, but not every day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב מרי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Someone who regularly eats mustard once every thirty days keeps illnesses out of his house. But not every day.
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching from the same speakers, built exactly like the lentil teaching, now about mustard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats: once a month is helpful and daily use is not. Mustard protects against illnesses in general, not one specific disease.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב מָרִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rav Mari said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who regularly eats mustard once in thirty days
keeps illnesses away from his house.
But every day — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב מָרִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָרָגִיל בְּחַרְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching to step 16, with the same structure, about mustard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mustard once every thirty days prevents illnesses in the home, but it should not be eaten daily.

steps.title: Why Not Eat Mustard Every Day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why mustard should not be eaten daily.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question as before, now about mustard. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks what harm daily mustard causes. The next step gives the answer.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the daily limit in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why mustard should not be eaten every day.

steps.title: Daily Mustard Weakens the Heart
steps.stepSummary: Eating mustard every day causes weakness of the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is harmful, causing weakness of the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that eating mustard daily weakens the heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As with lentils, the monthly benefit stays in place, and only daily use is a problem. Here the side effect is more serious: weakness of the heart.

phrases.english: Because it is harmful, causing weakness of the heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Daily mustard causes weakness of the heart.

steps.title: Small Fish Protect the Intestines and Strengthen the Whole Body
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אשי in the name of רב teaches that small fish prevent intestinal illness and also make the whole body flourish and stay healthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: Someone who regularly eats small fish will not suffer intestinal illness. And more than that, small fish make a person's whole body fruitful, help it grow, and keep it healthy.
steps.whatsHappening: A final health tip: small fish protect the intestines, and they also benefit the whole body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike lentils and mustard, there is no 'but not every day' limit here; regular eating is praised. The phrase ולא עוד אלא signals a step up, from one benefit (the intestines) to a benefit for the entire body.

keyTerms.meaning: Not only that, but even more

steps.whatToRemember: The pattern of this section: each food has a specific benefit, and some foods (lentils, mustard) help only in moderation, once a month. Small fish, though, are praised for regular eating.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two monthly foods. Lentils prevent אסכרה, and their daily harm is bad breath. Mustard prevents illnesses in general, and its daily harm is weakness of the heart.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
One who regularly eats small fish
will not come to suffer intestinal illness.
And not only that, but
small fish make fruitful and cause growth
and make healthy a person's entire body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב: הָרָגִיל בְּדָגִים קְטַנִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new health tip to the list, with no daily limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Regularly eating small fish prevents intestinal illness and benefits the whole body.

steps.title: Black cumin protects against heart pain
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that someone who regularly uses קצח will not suffer heart pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא, son of רבי חנינא, said: Someone who regularly uses black cumin will not come to have heart pain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more piece of health advice to the list. This one is about black cumin and the heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps listed foods that help or harm when eaten too often. Here the claim is simple: regular use of קצח protects the heart. This claim is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Black cumin, a spice used as medicine
One who is used to it, who does it regularly

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
One who is accustomed to black cumin
will not come to heart pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of health teachings about foods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Regular use of קצח prevents heart pain.

steps.title: Black cumin is called a deadly drug
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who calls קצח one of sixty deadly drugs. Someone who sleeps east of where it is stored is responsible for his own death.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that black cumin is one of the sixty deadly drugs. Someone who sleeps to the east of where it is stored has only himself to blame for his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חמא with a source that calls black cumin deadly. How can the same thing protect the heart?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חמא says קצח is healthy, and the ברייתא says it is dangerous. The detail about sleeping east of the storage area hints that the danger comes through the air. This is the key to the answer that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Its storage place, where it is piled up
His blood is on his own head; he is to blame for his death

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: קֶצַח — אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים סַמָּנֵי הַמָּוֶת הוּא,
phrases.english: Black cumin is one of the sixty deadly drugs,
and one who sleeps to the east of its storage pile,
phrases.notes: The west wind carries its smell eastward toward him.

phrases.english: his blood is on his own head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חמא's claim that קצח is good for the heart
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא calls קצח deadly. That seems to contradict calling it healthy.

steps.title: Smell harms, taste helps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about the smell of קצח, while רבי חמא is talking about its taste.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this source is talking about its smell, and that source is talking about its taste.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the two sources. Each one is talking about a different way of using קצח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breathing in the smell, as when sleeping downwind of a big pile, is dangerous. Tasting it in food helps the heart. So the two sources do not argue; they describe two different exposures.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one... that one (each source deals with a different case)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This one is about its smell, that one is about its taste.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be talking about the same use of קצח.
steps.terutzMaskana: The smell is dangerous; the taste is healing.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה's mother and the cumin bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה's mother would stick קצח onto his bread while baking it and then peel it off. He got the taste without the smell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה's mother used to bake bread for him. She would stick black cumin onto it and then peel it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story that shows the answer in real life. The taste soaked into the bread, and the spice itself was removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sticking the cumin on let its taste soak into the bread, which is the healthy part. Peeling it off removed the source of the harmful smell. This practice matches the 'taste vs. smell' answer exactly.

phrases.aramaic: אִימֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָפְיָא לֵיהּ רִיפְתָּא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya's mother would bake bread for him,
and she would stick it (the cumin) on it and peel it off.

steps.whatToRemember: With קצח, the smell is dangerous and the taste is healing. רבי ירמיה's mother found a way to get only the good part.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the answer of step 25 with a real practice.
steps.raayaObject: The split between taste and smell
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבי ירמיה's mother

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה on greens
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which quoted רבי יהודה's special ברכה for greens. רבי זירא (or רבי חיננא בר פפא) rules that the הלכה does not follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says the ברכה over greens is 'Who creates kinds of herbs.' רבי זירא said (and some say it was רבי חיננא בר פפא): The הלכה is not like רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The health section is over, and the גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה. It quotes רבי יהודה and gives a practical ruling against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה wanted a special, more specific ברכה for vegetables. The ruling is that we do not follow him in practice; we say בורא פרי האדמה. Even so, the next steps will explain his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who creates kinds of herbs,' רבי יהודה's ברכה for greens
The practical law is not (like this opinion)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: 'Who creates various kinds of herbs.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said, and some say Rabbi Chinana bar Pappa:
The halacha is not like Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, we say בורא פרי האדמה on vegetables, not a special ברכה for greens.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר בּוֹרֵא מִינֵי דְשָׁאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the health section and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה does not follow רבי יהודה's special ברכה for greens.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The same אמורא asks for the source behind רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said (and some say רבי חיננא בר פפא): What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה wanted a special ברכה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though we do not follow רבי יהודה in practice, the גמרא still wants to understand his logic. The question asks for a source, not for a new ruling.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said, and some say Rabbi Chinana bar Pappa:
What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion just rejected in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for a specific ברכה on each kind of food

steps.title: The פסוק: 'Blessed is ה׳ day by day'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the פסוק 'ברוך ה׳ יום יום' (תהלים סח:כ).
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'Blessed is ה׳, day by day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק as רבי יהודה's source. How the פסוק proves the point is explained in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'יום יום' (day by day) are the key. At this point we only have the verse; the explanation comes after a question about it.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'Blessed is the Lord, day by day.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.

steps.title: Do we only bless ה׳ by day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of the פסוק: surely we bless ה׳ at night too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that we bless Him by day and do not bless Him at night?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the plain meaning of the פסוק cannot be right. This pushes toward a deeper reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'day by day' could suggest blessing only in daytime, which is obviously wrong. This rhetorical question forces the verse to mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really so? (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: Is it so that by day we bless Him,
and at night we do not bless Him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal meaning of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We clearly bless ה׳ at night too, so 'by day' cannot be meant literally.

steps.title: Give each thing its fitting ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק means: each day, give ה׳ the ברכות that fit that day. The same applies to food: each kind gets the ברכה that fits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to tell you: each and every day, give Him the blessings that fit that day. Here too, for each and every kind of food, give Him the blessing that fits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the פסוק really teaches. It then applies that lesson to ברכות on food, which completes רבי יהודה's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Day by day' means each day gets its own fitting praise, such as on שבת or יום טוב. רבי יהודה extends this to food: greens deserve their own specific ברכה. That is why he says בורא מיני דשאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it comes to tell you

phrases.english: Rather, it is to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יוֹם וָיוֹם תֵּן לוֹ מֵעֵין בִּרְכוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: each and every day, give Him blessings that fit it,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי כׇּל מִין וּמִין תֵּן לוֹ מֵעֵין בִּרְכוֹתָיו.
phrases.english: here too, each and every kind, give Him blessings that fit it.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's idea is that every kind of food should get a ברכה that matches it. We do not rule like him for greens.
steps.confusionAlert: This step explains רבי יהודה's reasoning. It does not change the ruling from step 27 that the הלכה is not like him.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 30 and finishes the derivation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יום יום' seemed to limit blessing to daytime.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means each day, and so each kind of food, gets its own fitting ברכה.

steps.title: With ה׳, the full vessel holds more
steps.stepSummary: With people, an empty vessel holds things and a full one does not. With הקדוש ברוך הוא it is the opposite: a full vessel holds more, and an empty one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said (and some say רבי חיננא בר פפא): Come and see that the way of people is not like the way of הקדוש ברוך הוא. With people, an empty vessel holds things, and a full one does not. But הקדוש ברוך הוא is not like that: a full vessel holds more, and an empty one does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The same אמורא gives a new teaching, this time aggadic. It is about how spiritual knowledge grows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A physical cup that is full cannot take more. A person who is 'full' of Torah and good traits can take in even more, while an 'empty' person cannot hold what is given. The more you have, the more you can absorb.

keyTerms.meaning: The way of flesh and blood (human beings)

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said, and some say Rabbi Chinana bar Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that unlike the way of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the way of flesh and blood.
The way of flesh and blood:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלִי רֵיקָן מַחֲזִיק, מָלֵא אֵינוֹ מַחֲזִיק.
phrases.english: an empty vessel holds, a full one does not hold.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֵינוֹ כֵן,
phrases.english: But the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not so:
a full one holds, an empty one does not hold.

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same אמורא, linked to the previous one by his name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Spiritually, the one who is already full is the one who can hold more.

steps.title: The proof: 'If you listen, you will listen'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'אם שמוע תשמע' is read to mean: if you listen now, you will listen later; if not, you will not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And He said: If you will surely listen.' If you listen, you will listen. And if not, you will not listen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to support the 'full vessel' idea. The doubled word in the verse is read as two stages of listening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double verb שמוע תשמע is split: listening now leads to listening later. Someone who starts out 'full' keeps receiving, which is exactly the point of step 32.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introducing a פסוק)
Listen, you will listen (a doubled verb)

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And He said: If you will surely listen,'
if you listen, you will listen;
and if not, you will not listen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural basis for step 32.

steps.title: Another reading: review the old to gain the new
steps.stepSummary: A second reading: if you review what you already learned, you will understand new material. If you turn your heart away, you will no longer hear.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'If you listen' to the old, 'you will listen' to the new. And if your heart turns away, you will no longer hear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to read the same פסוק. This time it is about reviewing old learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמוע refers to old learning and תשמע to new learning. Reviewing keeps the 'vessel full,' so it can take in more. Turning away loses both. The last line borrows the words of the פסוק 'ואם יפנה לבבך' (דברים ל:יז).

keyTerms.meaning: In the old (what you already learned)

phrases.english: Another explanation:
If you listen to the old, you will listen to the new.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם יִפְנֶה לְבָבְךָ — שׁוּב לֹא תִשְׁמָע.
phrases.english: And if your heart turns away, you will no longer hear.

steps.whatToRemember: In Torah learning, whoever keeps reviewing and holding on can keep gaining more.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reviewing old learning lets you take in new learning; neglect closes you off.

steps.title: New משנה: when a wrong ברכה still counts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules on ברכות said by mistake. Saying בורא פרי האדמה on tree fruit counts. Saying בורא פרי העץ on ground produce does not count. Saying שהכל on anything counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone said 'Who creates fruit of the ground' over tree fruit, he has fulfilled his duty. If he said 'Who creates fruit of the tree' over produce of the ground, he has not. And over all foods, if he said 'by whose word all things came to be,' he has fulfilled his duty.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with someone who already said a ברכה that was not the exact right one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree grows from the ground, so the broader ברכה האדמה also covers tree fruit. Ground produce is not tree fruit, so העץ is wrong for it. שהכל is the most general ברכה and covers every food after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: By whose word all things came to be (the most general ברכה)

steps.confusionAlert: This is only about what counts after the fact (בדיעבד). Ideally, you should still say the correct, specific ברכה from the start.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a more general ברכה covers more specific foods after the fact, but a more specific one cannot cover something outside its category.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he blessed over fruits of the tree
'Who creates fruit of the ground,' he fulfilled his obligation.
And over produce of the earth,
'Who creates fruit of the tree,' he did not fulfill it.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כּוּלָּם, אִם אָמַר ״שֶׁהַכֹּל נִהְיֶה בִּדְבָרוֹ״ — יָצָא.
phrases.english: And over all of them, if he said 'by whose word all things came to be,' he fulfilled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the aggadic material.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the fact, האדמה covers tree fruit, העץ does not cover ground produce, and שהכל covers everything.

steps.title: Which תנא holds that a tree is basically part of the ground?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the main source of a tree is the earth. That view is what lets בורא פרי האדמה work on tree fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא who holds that the main part of a tree is the earth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking whose opinion the משנה follows when it says that בורא פרי האדמה works on tree fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if you say בורא פרי האדמה on tree fruit, you have still done your duty. That only makes sense if a tree counts as part of the ground. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Who is the תנא? Asks whose view the משנה follows
The main part or root source

phrases.english: GEMARA
Who is the tanna
that holds the main part of a tree is the earth?!
phrases.notes: This is the reason why 'האדמה' works on tree fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דְּעִיקַּר אִילָן אַרְעָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first ruling in the משנה from step 35.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a tree is basically part of the ground.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה, based on his view about ביכורים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the view belongs to רבי יהודה. He shows this from a משנה about ביכורים: even after the tree is cut down, רבי יהודה says the farmer still reads the passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is רבי יהודה. We learned in a משנה: If the spring dried up and the tree was cut down, the farmer brings the first fruits but does not read the passage. רבי יהודה says: He brings them and reads.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק names רבי יהודה as the תנא. He proves it from a case about ביכורים where the tree is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The farmer's reading thanks ה׳ for 'the land.' The תנא קמא holds that once the tree or spring is gone, the farmer cannot read it. רבי יהודה says he still reads, because the land is still there and the tree was only an extension of the land.

keyTerms.meaning: He brings the first fruits but does not read the passage
He brings the first fruits and reads the passage

steps.confusionAlert: 'Reading' here does not mean reading the תורה in general. It means the special thank-you passage said when bringing ביכורים, which mentions 'the land that You gave me.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This view explains why בורא פרי האדמה works on tree fruit: a tree is really part of the ground.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is Rabbi Yehuda,
as we learned in a mishna:
If the spring dried up and the tree was cut down
phrases.notes: This is after the first fruits were already picked.

phrases.english: he brings but does not read.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
He brings and reads.
phrases.notes: The land is still there, and the land is the main source.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה, who holds that the land is the main source of a tree.

steps.title: Why say that the tree blessing fails on ground produce? That is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second ruling of the משנה: בורא פרי העץ on ground produce does not count. It asks why this needs saying, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'On fruits of the ground,' and so on. But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה and challenges it as obvious and unneeded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ground produce clearly does not grow on trees. So of course a tree ברכה should not work for it. Why would the משנה bother to teach this?

keyTerms.meaning: Fruits of the ground (produce that does not grow on trees)
And so on; the rest of the quote
It is obvious! A challenge that a teaching is unneeded

phrases.english: "Over fruits of the ground," etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה: saying בורא פרי העץ does not count.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first ruling of the משנה to the second ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that בורא פרי העץ on ground produce does not count.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems too obvious to need teaching.

steps.title: The ruling is needed because רבי יהודה calls wheat a tree
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the ruling is needed only because of רבי יהודה, who holds that wheat is a kind of tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The ruling is needed only for רבי יהודה's view, since he said that wheat is a kind of tree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the 'obvious' challenge. He shows a view under which the ruling is not obvious at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wheat counts as a 'tree,' you might think בורא פרי העץ works on it. So the משנה must tell us that it does not. The source for רבי יהודה's view comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for... (shows when a ruling is not obvious)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is needed only according to Rabbi Yehuda,
who said that wheat is a type of tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 38.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the ruling is needed according to one view
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יהודה, wheat is a 'tree,' so the ruling is needed.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the tree אדם הראשון ate from: רבי מאיר says a vine
steps.stepSummary: To show that רבי יהודה calls wheat a tree, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about the tree that אדם הראשון ate from. It opens with רבי מאיר, who says it was a grapevine because wine brings sorrow.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: About the tree that אדם הראשון ate from, רבי מאיר says it was a grapevine. Nothing brings sorrow on a person like wine does, as the פסוק says: 'He drank from the wine and became drunk.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins bringing its proof. This step gives the setup of the ברייתא and the first opinion; רבי יהודה's view, the real proof, comes in step 42.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא in the ברייתא identifies the forbidden 'tree.' רבי מאיר links the sin to wine because wine causes trouble, as with נח. His view is not the proof itself; it sets up the list of opinions.

phrases.english: As we learned in a baraita:
The tree from which Adam, the first man, ate,
Rabbi Meir says: It was a vine,
for there is nothing

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמֵּבִיא יְלָלָה עַל הָאָדָם אֶלָּא יַיִן,
phrases.english: that brings wailing upon a person except wine,
as it is stated: "And he drank from the wine and became drunk."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא אִילָן שֶׁאָכַל מִמֶּנּוּ אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source for רבי יהודה's view mentioned in step 39.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה holds wheat is a kind of tree.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the tree of אדם הראשון.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה says it was a fig tree
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה says the tree was a fig tree. They fixed their mistake with the same thing they sinned with, since they sewed fig leaves to cover themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: It was a fig tree. The thing they ruined themselves with is the thing they were fixed with, as the פסוק says: 'They sewed fig leaves together.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion about the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה reasons that the leaves they used to cover themselves came from the same tree they sinned with. So the tree was a fig tree. This is still part of the list leading up to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says: It was a fig tree,
for with the thing by which they were ruined, they were fixed,
as it is stated: "And they sewed fig leaves."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tree of knowledge was a fig tree.

steps.title: רבי יהודה says it was wheat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the 'tree' was wheat, because a baby only starts to say 'Abba' and 'Imma' after tasting grain. This is the proof that he calls wheat a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: It was wheat. A baby does not know how to say 'Abba' and 'Imma' until he tastes grain.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the line the גמרא needed: רבי יהודה calls the 'tree' of knowledge wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat gives 'knowledge,' since a child starts to recognize his parents after eating grain. Because the פסוק calls it a 'tree,' רבי יהודה holds that wheat is a kind of tree. This completes the proof for step 39.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the משנה must teach that בורא פרי העץ does not work on wheat or other ground produce.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It was wheat,
for a baby does not know how to call out
"Father" and "Mother"
until he tastes the taste of grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third opinion in the ברייתא; it is the opinion that proves step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The tree of knowledge was wheat, so wheat is called a 'tree.'

steps.title: Tree blessing only where the branch stays and gives fruit again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the mistake one might make: since wheat is a 'tree,' it should get בורא פרי העץ. The משנה teaches otherwise. בורא פרי העץ is only for a plant whose branch stays after picking and gives fruit again.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since רבי יהודה said wheat is a kind of tree, we should say בורא פרי העץ on it. The משנה teaches us otherwise. When do we say בורא פרי העץ? When, after you take the fruit, the branch is still there and gives fruit again,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. It spells out the mistaken idea and gives the true rule for בורא פרי העץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being called a 'tree' in a story does not decide the ברכה. The test is practical: after picking, does the branch stay and grow fruit again? Wheat dies after harvest, so it cannot get בורא פרי העץ.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken first idea)

steps.whatToRemember: בורא פרי העץ is said only when the branch stays after picking and gives fruit again. Wheat does not fit this, so even for רבי יהודה it gets בורא פרי האדמה.
steps.confusionAlert: The text stops in the middle of the sentence. The contrast, that where the branch does not remain we say בורא פרי האדמה, comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: It would have entered your mind to say,
since Rabbi Yehuda said
wheat is a type of tree,
one should recite over it: "Who creates fruit of the tree."
So it teaches us:
Where do we recite "Who creates fruit of the tree"?
Where, when you take off the fruit,
the branch remains and produces again,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 39, using the proof from step 42.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the true test for בורא פרי העץ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wheat is a 'tree' for רבי יהודה, so it should get בורא פרי העץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: בורא פרי העץ is only for a plant whose branch stays and gives fruit again.
